name: 1337 Wallet
tagline: A professional EVM signer for developers, hackers, and advanced users.
elevatorPitch: Self-custody signer: understand the request, judge the risk, sign or reject. Easy RPC switching, hardware, LiFi swaps, and a fast terminal UI — no 1337 accounts, no analytics, no tracking server.
audience: Power users who manage their own RPCs and chains
Anyone who wants a serious signer without wallet bloat

differentiators: Confirm-time human summary, local simulation, and contract danger flags
Side panel + popup, multi-RPC per chain, network doctor
Seed, private key, Ledger, and Trezor in one shell
LiFi swaps, multi-send, MetaMask-compatible dapp provider
Normal vs Burner Mode signing — confirm every request, or mark a wallet as a disposable auto-signer
Dark terminal aesthetic inspired by 1337 Skulls
notA: Not a hosted wallet — keys never leave your browser except to chains you broadcast to
Not an analytics product — we do not track how you use the extension
Not a Foundry, Hardhat, or Etherscan replacement — no ABI playground, storage inspector, or cast-style utilities
Not a burner-only toy — suitable as a serious daily driver when hardened (Normal mode, auto-lock, hardware)

privacy.summary: 1337 Wallet does not run analytics, does not phone home to a tracking server, and does not create user profiles. Your vault, settings, and session live in Chrome extension storage on your machine.
storedLocally: Encrypted vault (seed / private keys) in chrome.storage.local
Wallet settings, custom RPCs, and chain preferences in chrome.storage.local
Unlocked session (active key metadata) in chrome.storage.session until lock or browser restart
networkWhenYouUseFeatures: Public RPC endpoints you choose (balances, sends, dapp reads)
LI.FI API when you open Swap or fetch routes (integrator id only; no 1337 backend)
Optional Etherscan-compatible API key you paste in Settings (sent to the explorer provider for tx history)
Ledger / Trezor device SDKs and Trezor Connect when you use hardware accounts
Token logos and chain metadata from public HTTPS URLs (e.g. LI.FI catalog)
neverCollected: Browsing history beyond what Chrome grants for dapp connection
Wallet addresses or balances sent to a 1337 database

chromeWebStore.singlePurpose: 1337 Wallet is a self-custody Ethereum (EVM) signer. Users create or import accounts, connect to dapps, review signing requests, and approve or reject them. Swaps, approvals, multisend, and hardware are the same purpose: the user authorizing their own crypto.

permissionJustifications.storage: Stores the encrypted vault (seed or private keys), accounts, settings, custom RPCs, and connected-site permissions in chrome.storage on this device. There is no 1337 cloud backup. storage is required so the wallet persists across sessions.
permissionJustifications.sidePanel: The wallet UI can open in Chrome's side panel so the user can keep a dapp and the signer visible at the same time. Users can switch to a toolbar popup in Settings. sidePanel only loads 1337's own page (index.html), not a panel on third-party sites.
permissionJustifications.scripting: Injects the in-page Ethereum provider (window.ethereum / EIP-6963) so websites can request accounts and signatures. Content scripts run at document_start on pages the user visits. Scripting is not used to scrape pages or run analytics.
permissionJustifications.host: Needed to (1) inject the dapp provider on sites the user visits, (2) call user-selected RPC endpoints and optional explorer or LI.FI APIs, and (3) talk to Trezor Connect (connect.trezor.io) when a Trezor is used. 1337 does not scrape browsing history and has no 1337 backend.

chromeWebStore.remoteCodeJustification: When the user connects a Trezor, @trezor/connect-webextension opens Trezor's official Connect UI from https://connect.trezor.io/9/ so keys stay on the device. That hosted UI is JavaScript not in our zip. Ledger uses WebHID with code bundled in the package. We do not load other remote scripts and we do not eval third-party strings. Popup and background bundles are in the uploaded package.
chromeWebStore.detailedDescription:
1337 is a self-custody EVM signer for developers, hackers, and power users. Understand the request, judge the risk, then sign or reject.

Why 1337
• Readable confirms — human summary, local simulation (pass / fail / revert / gas), and contract danger flags
• Easy RPC switching — 20+ chains, switch endpoints, network doctor
• Hardware — Ledger (WebHID) and Trezor Connect alongside seed and private-key accounts
• Signer tools — Signings history, Approvals (ERC-20 / NFT / Permit2), LiFi swaps, multisend, gas top-up, optional Inspect
• Normal or Burner Mode — confirm every request by default, or mark a software account as a disposable auto-signer with risk gates

Privacy
No analytics. No tracking server. No user accounts. Your encrypted vault stays in Chrome storage on this device. Network calls happen only when you use RPCs, swaps, explorers, or hardware. Policy: https://1337wallet.io/privacy

Self-custody
1337 is a tool, not a bank. You hold the keys. We do not guarantee, insure, or recover funds. Terms: https://1337wallet.io/terms

Works with MetaMask-compatible dapps (EIP-6963, optional window.ethereum).

Install: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/1337-wallet/ggdidobiifdhehiigbcjiddeeadklmhl
Discord: https://discord.gg/ZgADAzAKFd
Site: https://1337wallet.io/
